pr_title: Exception logging with Rails backtrace cleaner
pr_body:
Closes #5589.

Backtrace cleaning applies to exception logging and backtraces stored within the jobs.
pr_comments: Thank you! As you probably guessed, this will be in 7.1.

issue_context.title: Feature Suggestion: Exception logging with Rails backtrace cleaner
issue_context.body:
We have been running a small extension in our app that swaps the previous [Sidekiq::ExceptionHandler::Logger](https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/blob/fc7b7d8532549553673d4e510894b10a063792b3/lib/sidekiq/exception_handler.rb#L7) with our own, so that we can apply the [Rails backtrace cleaner](https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/BacktraceCleaner.html) to it and only log app specific lines.

This changed with Sidekiq v6.5.0 where [the default error handler was moved to a method in Sidekiq](https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/commit/67daa7a408b214d593100f782271ed108686c147#diff-2eecd3565b38823c09513903afa6686627d3ba8d883d520d3a83db61375e5ddeR63-R68), as part of the preparation for changes to Sidekiq 7. We can still wrap that method and apply the cleaner on our side, but I wanted to reach out and ask if this is maybe something that'd be interesting to have implemented in Sidekiq directly?

My thinking is that Sidekiq could provide some sort of hook / config for backtrace cleaning (e.g. `config[:backtrace_cleaner]`, a proc that receives the backtrace), that could be applied to this exception logging, and perhaps also to the backtraces stored within the jobs (similar to https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/issues/4451) if that'd be interesting too, and that within the [Rails context](https://github.com/mperham/sidekiq/blob/main/lib/sidekiq/rails.rb#L7) it could be set to the default `Rails.backtrace_cleaner` cleaner.

Would that be something of interest to have in Sidekiq itself? And I imagine this is something that'd be included only in the upcoming v7?

I'm happy to get a draft going, just wanted to start with some questions to gather initial interested and direction.

Thanks,
Carlos

review_comments: Nice, I hadn't gone this far into cleaning up the backtrace of jobs to store :+1:
Do you need to require this, just in case?

Seems like it is not necessary as it is always required. In newly created apps `rails` is required - https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq/blob/1813cbdbd5e2fff23bfed5488ebcf5c6eeebb2e2/myapp/config/application.rb#L3 and from there backtrace cleaner is loaded https://github.com/rails/rails/blob/9180e61802d1c025f15bf57db92f392400dce46a/railties/lib/rails.rb#L16
And even `rails` is already required from this file at the top.

Instead of aliasing the method, maybe we could wrap setting the config into a proc? e.g.

```ruby
config[:backtrace_cleaner] = -> backtrace { ::Rails.backtrace_cleaner.clean(backtrace) }
```
Cool, hopefully this should do it: https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq/pull/5796. Thanks again!

I was considering cleaning the backtrace when handling exceptions triggers an error too: https://github.com/fatkodima/sidekiq/blob/4a255eb6ff8299e0be1f3d13d46b9513e87aa6e8/lib/sidekiq/config.rb#L267-L270, would that make sense to do, or is it better to just let that log everything since it's likely an implementation issue there?
